source: KSQAAC Spardha Yashassu NMMS Study Material 2022, MAT Chapter 8 (questions: PDF pages 31-32, answers: PDF page 118)

questions.rule: A comes closest: the two signs in each row swap places, and < and > are turned round.
questions.working: In a mirror on the right, the two signs in each row change places and each one faces the other way. The rows ÷ +, < >, + − become + ÷, < >, − +. A has the first two rows right, but its bottom row is − ×.
questions.note: Hidden: no option is the exact mirror image. The bottom row should read − +, but A (the book's key) has − ×; B has > > in the middle row, and C and D are wrong in the top row.

questions.rule: The figure is the same on both sides, so its mirror image looks just like it.
questions.working: Each of the four arms of the cross has two tick marks and an arrowhead at the corner, so a mirror on the right leaves the figure looking the same.
questions.note: Hidden: the mirror image should look the same as the figure (two ticks on every arm), but no option does: each has three or four ticks on some arms, or arrowheads turned inwards. The book's key is B.

questions.rule: The letters swap sides and each one is flipped.
questions.working: In the mirror B stays at the top and G at the bottom, both flipped; the P moves to the left and the J to the right, both flipped.
questions.note: Hidden: options A and C are printed exactly the same, and both are the mirror image, so the question has two right answers (the book's key is A).

questions.rule: SCHOOL in a mirror: the letters in reverse order, each one flipped.
questions.working: The mirror shows L O O H C S from left to right, with the L, C and S turned round (O and H look the same). B leaves the C unflipped and D the L.
questions.note: Hidden: options A and C are printed exactly the same, and both are the correct mirror image, so the question has two right answers (the book's key is C).

questions.rule: B: the letters of CHILDREN in reverse order, each one flipped.
questions.working: In a mirror on the right, the last letter N comes first and every letter is turned round: N E R D L I H C, all flipped (I and H look the same). Only B has every letter flipped and in that order. A starts with the C, and C and D leave some letters unflipped.

questions.rule: A: the digits of 150847 in reverse order, each one flipped.
questions.working: The mirror shows the digits in reverse order, 7 4 8 0 5 1, with the 7, 4 and 5 turned round (0, 8 and 1 look the same). Only A turns all three: B leaves the 5 as it is, C the 7 and D the 4.

questions.rule: A: 39KXGB in reverse order, each character flipped.
questions.working: The mirror shows B G X K 9 3 from left to right, with the B, G, K, 9 and 3 turned round (X looks the same). Only A has every character flipped and in that order.

questions.rule: B: the two columns swap, and the dots move to the top-left.
questions.working: Mirroring swaps the columns: the triangle comes to the top-left and the square to the top-right, the circle to the bottom-left and the black hexagon to the bottom-right. The dots were on the top-right of the triangle and the circle, so in the mirror they are on the top-left. That is B. C still has the dots on the right; A and D do not swap the columns.

questions.rule: D: the two halves swap; the arrow points right, and the 7 and R are flipped with the dot on their left.
questions.working: In the mirror the half with the slanting line moves to the right and the line slopes the other way; the arrow in it now points right. The half with the 7 and R moves to the left, both characters flipped and the dot on their left. That is D. A and B keep the halves where they were; C keeps the slope and the dot as they were.

questions.rule: The mirror image starts at the top-right and ends with an arrow at the bottom-left pointing left.
questions.working: The curve starts with a ring at the top-left, bends down through a black dot and ends with an arrow at the bottom-right pointing right. In the mirror it starts at the top-right and ends at the bottom-left, pointing left.
questions.note: Hidden: no option is the mirror image. D has the right curve but with the ring and the black dot swapped; C (the book's key) has the ring and the dot right, but it is the figure turned a quarter turn, with the arrow pointing down.

questions.rule: A: the circle and square swap sides, and the two arrows are mirrored.
questions.working: In the mirror the square with the black corner moves to the bottom-left and the circle to the bottom-right. The arrow pointing up-left becomes one pointing up-right, on the left, and the arrow pointing right becomes one pointing left, on the right. That is A. B's right-hand arrow points right, C keeps the circle and square where they were, and D has the black corner in the circle.
questions.note: In the book's drawing, A's left-pointing arrow slopes slightly down instead of slightly up. It is still the only option that is the mirror image.

questions.rule: B: the top arm now bends left, the bottom arm right, and the double arrowhead moves to the left.
questions.working: Mirroring turns every arrow round. At the top the line bent to the right, so in the mirror it bends to the left; at the bottom it bent left, so now it bends right. The middle line had its double arrowhead on the right; now it is on the left. Only B has all three: C keeps the double arrowhead on the right, and A and D keep the bends as they were.

questions.rule: The circle and square swap sides, and the extra arrowheads move to the other diagonal.
questions.working: In the mirror the square moves to the right and the circle to the left. The diagonal with the extra arrowheads ran from bottom-left to top-right; in the mirror it runs from top-left to bottom-right.
questions.note: Hidden: options A and C are printed exactly the same, and both are the mirror image, so the question has two right answers (the book's key is C).

questions.rule: B: the diamond and circle at the top swap sides, and so do the square and circle at the bottom.
questions.working: The figure has a circle at the top-left and a diamond at the top-right, a square at the bottom-left and a circle at the bottom-right. In the mirror each moves to the other side: diamond top-left, circle top-right, circle bottom-left, square bottom-right. That is B.

questions.rule: D: the brackets are mirrored, and the two arrows still point at each other.
questions.working: Each bracket's top end turned left and its bottom end right; in the mirror the top turns right and the bottom left. The two arrows point towards each other, and in a mirror they still do. Only D has both: A and B keep the brackets as they were, and C has the arrows pointing away from each other.
